title: Survey Finds AI-Generated Code Increases Debugging and Failure Rates and Creates a Comprehension Gap
gist: A Coleman Parkes survey for Undo of 300 senior engineering leaders, mostly in C/C++ mission-critical software, finds AI coding agents have moved the bottleneck to debugging and comprehension: 16.9 hours per week debugging versus 9.8 producing code, and 35% of generated code reaching production not fully understood. Overall release cycles are reported as no faster. Note the sponsor sells AI root-cause analysis.

insights.claim: In the surveyed teams, engineers spend an average of 9.8 hours per week producing code but 16.9 hours per week debugging issues, equal to 42% of the average working week.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: The AI coding speedup is being offset by debugging time in complex codebases.
insights.quote: teams spend an average of 9.8 hours per week producing code, but 16.9 hours per week debugging issues

insights.claim: The survey of 300 senior engineer leaders working on mission-critical software, mostly C/C++, was run by Coleman Parkes on behalf of Undo, a vendor of AI-powered root-cause analysis.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Sponsor and sample (C/C++, mission-critical) limit how far results generalize.
insights.locator: A survey conducted by independent research firm Coleman Parkes

insights.claim: 79% of engineering leaders say AI agents generate code significantly faster, but effort shifted to debugging and unpicking that code leaves the overall release cycle no faster than before.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Local code-generation gains may not translate into end-to-end delivery speed.

insights.claim: As AI generates most code, engineers lack the inherent understanding they used to have, so defects escape more easily and nobody can trace failures to root cause.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Comprehension debt becomes a hidden cost of agentic coding.
insights.quote: Now that AI is generating most of the code being produced, engineers no longer have the inherent understanding they used to.

insights.claim: 35% of generated code reaches production before the team has fully understood it, and 80% of respondents say coding agents struggle with difficult problems in complex codebases.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Review capacity, not generation, is the constraint on safe adoption.
insights.locator: Due to the acceleration in code generation

insights.claim: About one-third of teams use AI agents for comprehension and debugging only in straightforward codebases, relying on other techniques for complex systems.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Agent use is limited by trust in complex code.

insights.claim: In the previous six months 81% of teams had at least one production incident or outage (14% multiple times per month), 93% had incorrect root-cause diagnosis from hallucination at least once (18% multiple times per month), and 91% had test escapes (8% multiple times per month).
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: AI-assisted diagnosis hallucination is widespread, supporting demand for deterministic debugging tools.

insights.claim: Undo's Greg Law said engineers lose days unraveling code that is almost but not quite right, and that agents are great at writing reams of code but less capable at debugging it.
insights.speaker: Greg Law
insights.so_what: Vendor statement positioning debugging as the next agent-tooling market.
insights.quote: while agents are great at writing reams of code quickly, they're less capable at debugging it
insights.locator: Greg Law, founder and CEO of Undo

insights.claim: The broader consensus is that AI agents do not change the nature of software engineering, which is about understanding constraints, making trade-offs and ensuring the system behaves as intended, and approaches such as the test-first red-green loop are used to manage agent speed outpacing review.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Human understanding and verification remain the scarce resource.
insights.locator: Since the launch and widespread adoption
